div.head: IV Eg 1.2
div.ab: gif he þonne gelomlice þurh his bydelas his gafoles myngað, ⁊ he þonne aheardað ⁊ hit þencð to ætstrengenne, wen is, þæt þæs hlafordes grama to ðan swiðe weaxe, þæt he him ne unne naðer ne æhta ne lifes:

gyf he ðonne gelomlice þurh his bydelas his gafoles myngað, ⁊ he ðonne aheardað ⁊ hit þencð to ætstrengenne, wen is, þæt ðæs hlafordes grama to ðam swyðe weaxe, þæt he him ne unne naðer ne æhta ne lifes:

si uero frequenter hęc eadem per suos precones requisierit, et ille exasperatus et ad iracundiam prouocatus opera sua iniqua per uim defendere uoluerit, credendum procul dubio, flammam indignationis domini aduersus huiusmodi hominem in tantum accendi debere, ut nec illum aliqua possessione nec ętiam uita dignum existimet ęssę:

Gyf he ðonne gelomlice þurh his bydelas his gafoles myngað ⁊ he ðonne aheardað ⁊ hit þencð to ætstrengenne, wen is, þæt ðæs hlafordes grama to ðam swyðe weaxe, þæt he him ne unne naðer ne æhta ne lifes:

wenn er jedoch oftmals durch seine Büttel um seine Abgabe mahnt, indem jener dann hartnäckig wird und es zu ertrotzen meint, so ist Wahrscheinlichkeit, dass des Herrn Zorn bis zu dem [Grade] stark anwachse, dass er jenem weder Besitz, noch Leben lässt:

but if he often demands his rent through his beadles, and the other then grows obstinate and thinks to hold out against it, it is likely that the lord's anger will grow so great that he will leave him neither possessions nor life:

If, however, through his bailiffs he repeatedly claims his rent, and the tenant proves obstinate, and thinks to stand out against it, it is to be expected that the lord's anger will grow so great that he will grant him neither property nor life.

If, however, he frequently through his bailiffs demands his rent, and the other then proves obstinate and intends to withhold it with defiance, it is to be expected that the lord’s anger will so increase that he may grant him neither possessions nor life.
div.note: BF: added from Gesetze I p. 206, October 2026 (MS C (Latin)); O: corrected against Gesetze I, October 2026 (was “(Latin version of C)”, now “∅ (moved to BF)”)

note.seg: Nicht bloss ‘messengers’, da der Herr laut des Folgenden Gerichtsbarkeit übt, sondern niedere Beamte zum Geldeintreiben; s. Gl Büttel 2. 3
Not merely ‘messengers’, since according to what follows the lord exercises jurisdiction, but minor officials for collecting money; see Gl Büttel 2. 3

‘hínzuziehen’ Schmid zu frei; genauer, doch ohne Objekt, ‘resist’ Thorpe; ‘deforce, withhold wrongfully’ Toller Suppl. ohne sonstigen Beleg. Die Versio ist genau; strengan, strangian heisst ‘stark machen’

‘hínzuziehen’ Schmid, too free; more precisely, but without an object, ‘resist’ Thorpe; ‘deforce, withhold wrongfully’ Toller Suppl., without any other instance. The Versio is exact; strengan, strangian means ‘to make strong’
Versio führt ein Bild wohl aus Jesa. 66, 15 ein
The Versio introduces an image, probably from Isa. 66, 15

Habe, einschliesslich des Bauerguts. Dass ein säumiger Abgabenzahler vom Grundherrn getötet werden dürfe, war nicht Agsächs. Recht, sondern Erfindung des Pfaffen, der die Zehntpflicht einschärfen will

Property, including the peasant holding. That a defaulting payer of dues might be killed by the lord of the manor was not Anglo-Saxon law but the invention of the cleric who wishes to enforce the duty of paying tithe
See Andrews, Old English Manor, pp. 142–3.
The Latin version translates per vim defendere which Liebermann regards as nearer the meaning than Toller’s suggestion ‘to withhold wrongfully’ (see Suppl. p. 24, s.v. ætstrengan).
Perhaps not to be taken too literally.
